skill.name: tilt
skill.description: Check Tilt deployment health, inspect logs, handle Docker Compose health gaps, and improve Tiltfiles for local development workflows.
skill.summary: Guide AI agents through Tilt health checks, logs, lifecycle commands, and Tiltfile authoring.
skill.author: 0xBigBoss

security_audit.summary: Several Markdown backtick detections are false positives, but command examples intentionally guide agents to run local Tilt, Docker, git, jq, and zmx commands. The main concern is state-changing Tilt lifecycle operations, especially trigger, up, and down, which should require explicit user approval. I found no prompt injection or hidden data-exfiltration intent in SKILL.md, CLI_REFERENCE.md, or TILTFILE_API.md.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running tilt trigger, tilt up, tilt down, or commands that change cluster resources.

remediation.issue: Shell examples use local project names and zmx sessions
remediation.suggestion: Keep variable expansions quoted and avoid eval or untrusted command construction when adapting the examples.

remediation.issue: Command examples can look like automatic actions
remediation.suggestion: Document which commands are read-only and which commands modify local resources.

content.value_statement: Local Tilt environments can hide failing resources, stale logs, and Docker Compose health problems. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through status checks, logs, and Tiltfile fixes.
actual_capabilities: Query Tilt UIResource status and summarize runtime and update health.
Surface build errors before pending or in-progress resources.
Identify Docker Compose healthcheck failures missed by basic Tilt status fields.
Read and filter Tilt logs by resource, time range, tail count, and JSON output.
Guide Tiltfile authoring for resources, live update, configuration, extensions, and UI links.
Start or reuse a zmx session for tilt up using the project name.
limitations: Requires local Tilt and project tools to be installed.
Commands inspect the current workstation and active development cluster.
Examples do not replace production deployment policy review.
Tiltfile examples need project-specific validation before use.

use_cases.title: Check Local Deployment Health
use_cases.description: Find failing Tilt resources, pending updates, and Docker Compose healthcheck problems after a code change.

use_cases.title: Triage Build And Runtime Errors
use_cases.description: Use status queries and recent logs to identify why a local service did not reach a ready state.

use_cases.title: Improve Tiltfile Workflows
use_cases.description: Review Tiltfile resource definitions, live update ordering, dependency links, and UI labels.

prompt_templates.title: Run A Health Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for a local Tilt environment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this Tilt environment for errors first. Summarize failing resources, pending resources, and Docker Compose health issues. Ask before running commands that change state.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate One Resource
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused troubleshooting for a specific resource.
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate the <resource> Tilt resource. Use status and recent logs. Explain the likely cause and the next verification step.

prompt_templates.title: Review A Tiltfile
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a Tiltfile without changing unrelated behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Tiltfile for dependency order, live update steps, trigger modes, and resource labels. Suggest minimal changes with clear reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Troubleshooting Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced investigation on a custom Tilt port.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a troubleshooting flow for intermittent Tilt failures on port <port>. Include status polling, log filters, Docker Compose health checks, and valid restart cases.

output_examples.input: Check Tilt health for the current project.
output: No runtime errors found. One resource is still in progress, so recheck before declaring success.
One Docker Compose service reports an unhealthy healthcheck. Inspect the probe output next.

output_examples.input: Investigate why the api resource is not ready.
output: The latest build failed before deployment completed.
Recent logs point to a missing dependency during startup.
Verify the dependency and trigger a rebuild after approval.

output_examples.input: Review this Tiltfile for faster local updates.
output: Move rebuild triggers before sync steps in the live update list.
Add labels to group backend and frontend resources.
Keep manual trigger mode for expensive builds.

best_practices: Check error states before broad pending status lists.
Re-poll resources that are in progress before reporting success.
Use structured Tilt output when you need reliable status decisions.
anti_patterns: Declaring a deployment healthy while resources are still pending or in progress.
Restarting Tilt for normal code or Tiltfile changes.
Ignoring Docker Compose healthStatus because runtimeStatus is ok.

faq.question: Does this skill run Tilt automatically?
faq.answer: It provides command guidance. The assistant should ask before commands that change local resources.

faq.question: Can it work with non-default Tilt ports?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for passing a custom port to Tilt commands.

faq.question: What tools are expected?
faq.answer: Tilt is required. jq, rg, docker, kubectl, and zmx are useful for some workflows.

faq.question: Can it help edit Tiltfiles?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide edits for resources, live update, dependencies, configuration, and UI links.

faq.question: Does it cover Docker Compose?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights Docker Compose healthcheck signals that basic Tilt status can miss.

faq.question: Is it intended for production clusters?
faq.answer: No. It is focused on local development. Review context and permissions before using shared clusters.
